mem.t: He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers; for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,

lessons.title: The Gift of the Fivefold Ministry
lessons.theme: The ascended Christ gives five kinds of servants to his church

v: But to each one of us, the grace was given according to the measure of the gift of Christ.
He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers;
for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving, to the building up of the body of Christ,
until we all attain to the unity of the faith and of the knowledge of the Son of God, to a full grown man, to the measure of the stature of the fullness of Christ,

lessons.still: Quietly call to mind the people who have led you in life: the one who brought you to faith, the one who taught you to read the Bible, the one who shepherded you, the one who pointed you in the right direction. Name them one by one, and give thanks to God for each of them.
teach: A football team has strikers, midfielders, defenders and a goalkeeper. Each has a position, and each sees the game from a different angle: the striker spots the chance to attack, the defender spots the gap at the back. A team made up entirely of strikers would fall apart. What Christ has given his church is likewise a complete line-up.

Verse 7 says that each of us has received grace according to the measure of Christ’s gift. Verse 11 names five kinds of people Christ has given: apostles pioneer and lay foundations; prophets discern and declare the mind of God; evangelists bring people to the Lord; shepherds care for and feed the flock; teachers make the truth plain. Notice the subject of the sentence: “he gave.” These ministries are gifts from the ascended Christ, not titles people compete for.

The fivefold ministry is not five ranks but five perspectives, and no single person can represent the whole Christ alone. A shift in mindset: stop asking “Who is the greatest?” and start asking “Which perspective are we missing?” If our fellowship, small group or ministry team has only one voice, we need to ask the Lord to supply the other gifts.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The “5” in 235 is our fellow soldiers of the fivefold ministry. God’s kingdom system does not rest on one super-leader; it rests on Christ as the Head and the five ministries working together. When we let Jesus reign, ministry does not turn into power; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, ministry does not turn into status.
q: Who is God? — Christ himself gives ministries to the church. What kind of Head does this show you?
Who am I? — Of the five perspectives, which comes most naturally to you? Which is most lacking in you?
How shall I respond? — Which person who has led you will you thank and pray for?
lessons.jesus: Jesus alone holds all five ministries perfectly. He is the Apostle sent by the Father, he is the Prophet, he preached the good news of the kingdom, he is the Good Shepherd, and he is the Teacher his disciples called “Rabbi.” The fivefold ministry of the church exists to display the whole Christ on earth.
lessons.pray: Ascended Lord Jesus, thank you for giving apostles, prophets, evangelists, shepherds and teachers to your church. Help me to honour every gift and not to mistake my own perspective for the whole picture. Place me where you have appointed me, so that with my fellow soldiers I may build up your body. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write a letter or send a message thanking someone who has shepherded or taught you
Write down which of the five perspectives comes most naturally to you
Pray for your church’s leadership team, naming each person
lessons.noon: “He gave some to be apostles; and some, prophets; and some, evangelists; and some, shepherds and teachers” — Lord, thank you right now for giving us grace in its fullness.

lessons.title: Equipping the Saints for Their Work
lessons.theme: Ministry exists not to do everything but to equip the saints

v: Moses’ father-in-law said to him, “The thing that you do is not good.
You will surely wear away, both you, and this people that is with you; for the thing is too heavy for you. You are not able to perform it yourself alone.

from whom all the body, being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part, makes the body increase to the building up of itself in love.

lessons.still: Think of one thing you have always felt is “quicker if I just do it myself.” Quietly lay it before the Lord and ask, “Lord, who do you want me to hand this to, and who do you want me to teach?” Wait a moment, and write down any names that come to mind.
teach: Moses sat alone judging the people from morning till evening, while the queue stood waiting all day long. His father-in-law Jethro put his finger right on it: “The thing that you do is not good.” Not because Moses lacked spirituality or effort, but because he had confused “I can do this” with “I should do this.” The result: he was worn out, and so were the people.

Ephesians 4:12 says the fivefold ministry is “for the perfecting of the saints, to the work of serving.” The word translated “perfecting” carries the sense of mending fishing nets or setting broken bones: equipping people and putting them back in their proper place. Verse 16 pictures the outcome: the whole body fitted and knit together, every joint doing its part, each helping the other, and the body growing as it builds itself up in love. A leader’s success is measured not by how much they do themselves, but by how many people they equip.

Doing everything ourselves is often hidden self-rule: we fear others will do it badly, we cannot let go of the feeling of being needed, we want to stay in control. Equipping the saints takes humility, laying down power and returning to our place. A shift in mindset: from “Watch me do it,” to “Let me do it with you,” to “You go and do it, and I’ll support you from behind.” This is exactly the path of multiplication.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Life first, then relationships, then ministry. Equipping is not handing out tasks; it is a life walking alongside a life. Humility draws out humility: when leaders are willing to let go, the saints are willing to take up responsibility. When everyone does their part, God’s kingdom system is built up.
q: Who is God? — God corrected Moses through Jethro’s words. What does this show you about the way he shepherds?
Who am I? — In what area are you “performing it yourself alone,” leaving yourself and others worn out?
How shall I respond? — This week, what one task will you teach one of your spiritual children to do?
lessons.jesus: For three years Jesus walked with the Twelve: first he let them watch, then he had them do it with him, then he sent them out, and when they came back they reviewed it together. In the end he entrusted the Great Commission to these once-weak men. He is the perfect model of equipping the saints.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that I often do everything myself, because I want control and I want to be needed. Tear down my self-rule and give me a heart to equip others. Teach me to walk alongside, to teach and to let go, so that your body may do its work and grow up in love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: List one area of service you could hand over to someone else
Spend fifteen minutes showing a brother or sister how to do something, and do it together
Tell a co-worker who is willing to step up, “I believe you can do this.”
lessons.noon: “Being fitted and knit together through that which every joint supplies, according to the working in measure of each individual part” — Lord, right now let me equip others rather than do it all myself.

lessons.title: Working as a Team
lessons.theme: The Holy Spirit speaks in a team that serves the Lord with one heart

v: Now in the assembly that was at Antioch there were some prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
As they served the Lord and fasted, the Holy Spirit said, “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them.”
Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away.

lessons.still: Picture yourself sitting in a circle with your co-workers, not for a meeting but to minister to the Lord and wait on him together. Be still for a moment and say to him, “Holy Spirit, please speak among us.”
teach: When geese migrate over long distances they fly in a V formation. When the lead goose tires, it drops back and another takes its place. One goose cannot fly far, but a flock can cross mountains and seas. The work of God’s kingdom is the same: a journey in which a group of people take turns carrying the load and hold one another up.

The leadership team at Antioch was remarkably diverse. Barnabas was a Levite born in Cyprus; Simeon was called Niger (meaning “black”); Lucius came from Cyrene in North Africa; Manaen had grown up with Herod the tetrarch; and Saul had once been a Pharisee who persecuted the church. People of very different backgrounds “served the Lord and fasted” together. And it was in such a team that the Holy Spirit spoke and sent out Barnabas and Saul.

At the heart of teamwork is not a rota of tasks but waiting on the Lord with one heart. God first, then people, then the work: a team worships together first, then decides together. Sending is also the team’s work: those who lay on hands and those who are sent share the burden together. Any small group or ministry team today can become an “Antioch.”
lessons.light: 321 Light: The Holy Spirit is my guide, not some strong personality. Only when everyone on the team lives the self-emptied life can we hear the same voice; only when everyone is humble can we be one amid our differences. That is what fellow soldiers are: not just people who do things together, but people who serve the Lord together.
q: Who is God? — The Holy Spirit spoke while a diverse team was worshipping. What does this show you about how he works?
Who am I? — On a team, do you tend to insist on your own opinion, or can you wait on the Lord with others?
How shall I respond? — Next time your team meets, how much time could you spend worshipping and praying together first?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus sent out his disciples, he sent them “two by two.” He never shaped lone heroes; he built teams who walk together. He himself said that the Son can do nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing.
lessons.pray: Holy Spirit, make our team minister to the Lord first, and only then do the Lord’s work. Tear down the competition and comparison among us, and let people of different backgrounds and gifts wait on you with one heart. When you speak, we will obey; when you send, we will go together. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Next time your team meets, suggest praying together for ten minutes first
Pray for the co-worker on your team who is most different from you
Ask a co-worker, “How can I support you these days?”
lessons.noon: “Separate Barnabas and Saul for me, for the work to which I have called them” — Lord, right now let me hear where you are sending me.

lessons.title: Working Together in Harmony
lessons.theme: The one who plants and the one who waters are the same; we are God’s fellow workers

v: I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase.
So then neither he who plants is anything, nor he who waters, but God who gives the increase.
Now he who plants and he who waters are the same, but each will receive his own reward according to his own labor.
For we are God’s fellow workers. You are God’s farming, God’s building.

lessons.still: Think of someone who serves alongside you, and thank the Lord for them: “Lord, thank you for giving me this co-worker. They can do what I cannot.” Let gratitude take the place of comparison.
teach: In a symphony the violins carry the melody, the cellos hold down the bass, and the timpani sound only now and then. If every player insisted on playing the melody, all you would have is noise. True teamwork means knowing when to play and when to rest, when to stand in front and when to hold others up from behind.

The Corinthians said, “I follow Paul,” and “I follow Apollos,” turning co-workers into factions. But Paul said: I planted, Apollos watered, but God gave the increase; the one who plants and the one who waters are the same. The secret of working together lies in verse 9: we are “God’s fellow workers.” When the focus shifts from “Who gets the credit?” to “What is God doing?”, co-workers no longer need to compare themselves with one another.

Working together means accepting different rhythms. Pioneers move fast; shepherds move steadily. Prophetic people speak bluntly; pastoral people are considerate. Different does not mean right or wrong; it means complementary. Partnership begins when I appreciate other people’s gifts instead of trying to remake them in my image. Each will receive a reward according to their own labour, so there is no need to grab someone else’s.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride provokes pride, and both sides lose; humility draws out humility, and both sides win. The key to working together is focus: when our focus is on Jesus, co-workers are comrades; when our focus is on ourselves, co-workers become rivals. When the glory goes to God, there is no need to fight over credit.
q: Who is God? — “God who gives the increase.” How does this shape the way you see the fruit of your service?
Who am I? — Have you ever quietly compared yourself with a co-worker, or tried to make someone more like you?
How shall I respond? — How will you concretely show appreciation to a co-worker who is very different from you?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said that the one who reaps gathers fruit to eternal life, “that both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.” He values the one who sows as much as the one who reaps. In his eyes, others laboured and we reap, and it is all part of one harvest.
lessons.pray: Lord, we are your fellow workers. Remove from my heart every thought of comparison and competing for credit. Make me glad to plant and glad to water, glad to stand in front and glad to stand behind. Let all the growth be credited to you and all the glory be given to you. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Tell a co-worker face to face that you value a gift in them that you do not have
In one area of service, deliberately take a supporting role so that someone else can flourish
Pray a blessing over a co-worker you have disagreed with
lessons.noon: “For we are God’s fellow workers” — Lord, right now let me work with one heart, with you and with my brothers and sisters.

lessons.title: Building Up the Body of Christ
lessons.theme: We are all living stones, built together into a dwelling place for God

v: Come to him, a living stone, rejected indeed by men, but chosen by God, precious.
You also as living stones are built up as a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
in whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.

lessons.still: Imagine you are a stone, picked up by the Lord’s hand, shaped and set into a wall, pressed close against the stones beside you. Quietly say, “Lord, put me in the place you want me.”
teach: Stones scattered on the ground are just stones, however fine the material. Only when a builder lays them one by one, each bearing weight and supporting the others, do they become a house. However beautiful a single stone may be, no one can live in it. God wants not just a lot of good Christians, but a spiritual home.

Peter calls the Lord “a living stone,” rejected by people yet chosen by God and precious. As we come to him, we too become living stones, built up into a spiritual house. Paul says we are “built together” into a dwelling place for God in the Spirit. The word “together” is the key: God’s dwelling is not found in one person, but among many people joined to one another.

This week we have seen the fivefold ministry (Day 1), equipping the saints (Day 2), working as a team (Day 3) and working together in harmony (Day 4). Today we see the goal: building up the body of Christ. Next week we face a fact: everyone who builds God’s house will meet spiritual attack, and so we must put on the full armour God provides.
lessons.light: 321 Light: One purpose: to build what belongs to God, God’s kingdom system. That system is not an organisational chart; it is a spiritual house with Christ as the cornerstone and all the saints as living stones. When we let Jesus reign, this house belongs to God; when we let Jesus receive all the glory, this house is filled with God’s presence.
q: Who is God? — The stone people rejected became God’s precious living stone. What kind of Lord does this show you?
Who am I? — Are you a stone sitting off by yourself, or a living stone willing to be built into the wall?
How shall I respond? — With which fellow soldiers will you share the responsibility of building?
lessons.jesus: Jesus said, “On this rock I will build my assembly.” He is the builder, and he is also the cornerstone. We do not build the church for Jesus; we are built by him and work alongside him. He is still building today, until his bride is made ready.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you are the living stone and the cornerstone. I come to you willing to be shaped and built by you. Join me together with my fellow soldiers, so that we become a dwelling place of God in the Spirit, and let your house be filled with your glory. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Write down the names of three fellow soldiers and pray for them
Meet with a co-worker and share your gifts and burdens with each other
At a gathering this week, take the initiative on one small task that builds others up
lessons.noon: “In whom you also are built together for a habitation of God in the Spirit.” — Lord, right now build me into your house.
